purpose: Decide the dipolar branch: does a usable separation window exist (U gain outruns f loss) or not (f loss dominates)?
the_one_exponent: f decay length λ_f vs U rise exponent p; net figure N(d)=U·f^α (α=0.5 for g∝√f) rising ⇒ open, falling ⇒ closed.

f_falls_slowly (\u03bb=2.0nm).interpretation: U gain outruns f loss → dipolar window OPEN (larger d favorable)
f_falls_slowly (\u03bb=2.0nm).caveat: Inputs are tier 'saturation_model', NOT GW-BSE — illustrative, not a verdict.

f_falls_fast (\u03bb=0.25nm).interpretation: f loss dominates U gain → dipolar window CLOSED (branch shuts)
f_falls_fast (\u03bb=0.25nm).caveat: Inputs are tier 'saturation_model', NOT GW-BSE — illustrative, not a verdict.

one_point_guard.reason: need ≥2 (d,U,f) points; have 1. One point cannot give a slope — this is exactly the gap the geometric prior leaves open.

flagship_gwbse_dsweep: not yet computed — run the heterobilayer GW-BSE at ≥2 interlayer separations (phase2_gwbse_dsweep.json). This is the branch-deciding run.
rigor: Self-test inputs are illustrative (tier saturation_model). The real verdict requires GW-BSE U and oscillator strength f at ≥2 separations; until then the 209-shortlist ranking's favorable-tradeoff ASSUMPTION is untested.
